ppi_focus: Warm-gearbox test drive: shift quality into 2nd and 3rd, grinding, and popping out of gear under decel; check the gearbox oil for metal on the fill plug.
Clutch: slip in 4th–6th under load, engagement height, hydraulic leaks at the master and slave cylinders.
Cabin water: lift the footwell carpets, check the seat-rail bolts for corrosion, clear and test both soft-top drains.
Soft-top fabric at the rear-corner fold points, header seal and seams.
Water pump weep hole and coolant crust; valve cover, front crank seal and diff pinion/output seals.
Skid plate and bracket security (recall 19V496000), plus a VIN recall check at the dealer.
Tire DOT dates, tread wear pattern (shoulder wear suggests track use), battery test.
Suspension: end links, lower control arm bushings, rear subframe noises; alignment check.
Mazda Connect screen for delamination or ghost touches; scan for stored codes.
Paint meter for respray on the aluminum hood, trunk and fenders; nose chip damage and PPF.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a clean history report plus dated invoices showing time-based service, including brake fluid.
Up: a later build month or documented warranty gearbox replacement, plus a clean PPI with a quiet, crisp warm shift.
Up: a negotiated price nearer the profile's Sport band, with an itemised out-the-door figure.
Down: grinding or synchro wear, cabin water damage, a branded title, or track-use evidence found at the PPI.
Down: the dealer refuses an independent PPI or will not share the history report.
evidence.mission_note: A manual ND Miata in California is a direct enthusiast-bridge fit and resells easily. Being an early 2016 6MT with no captured records, its fit depends on gearbox evidence and a PPI.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity: the VIN decodes to a 2016 MX-5 Sport 2.0L soft top. It also states a 6-speed manual, 31,993 miles, a $20,875 asking price after a $120 reduction, and an Autotrader no-accidents badge. Only the search card was captured, so title, owners, records, colours and photos are not established rather than shown to be absent. Nothing is observed wrong. The open items are model-specific: the early-2016 6MT gearbox has the highest failure-rate risk, and there is no transmission or build-date evidence. Time-based maintenance is unproven on a ~10-year-old, low-use car. Two applicable recalls (skid plate 19V496000, airbag module 24V695000) have unknown completion status. On price, the asking figure falls inside the computed fair-value range, but that range leans on Club/GT and low-mile comps. Against the profile's Sport band and the 2017 Sport peer at $20,500, it sits at the upper end for this spec.
evidence.next_action: Ask Atlas Auto Mall for the history report, a door-jamb build-date photo, any service and recall records, tire date codes, an itemised out-the-door price, and confirmation that an independent PPI in Orange County is allowed.
